395: void VehicleCmdGate::publishControlCommands(const Commands & commands)
396: {
397:   // Check system emergency
398:   if (use_emergency_handling_ && is_emergency_state_heartbeat_timeout_) {
399:     return;
400:   }
401: 
402:   // Check external emergency stop
403:   if (is_external_emergency_stop_) {
404:     return;
405:   }
406: 
407:   // Check initialization is done
408:   if (!isDataReady()) {
409:     return;
410:   }
411: 
412:   Commands filtered_commands;
413: 
414:   // Set default commands
415:   {
416:     filtered_commands.control = commands.control;
417:     filtered_commands.gear = commands.gear;  // tmp
418:   }
419: 
420:   if (moderate_stop_interface_->is_stop_requested()) {  // if stop requested, stop the vehicle
421:     filtered_commands.control.longitudinal.speed = 0.0;
422:     filtered_commands.control.longitudinal.acceleration = moderate_stop_service_acceleration_;
423:   }
424: 
425:   // Check emergency
426:   if (use_emergency_handling_ && is_system_emergency_) {
427:     RCLCPP_WARN_THROTTLE(
428:       get_logger(), *get_clock(), std::chrono::milliseconds(1000).count(), "Emergency!");
429:     filtered_commands.control = emergency_commands_.control;
430:     filtered_commands.gear = emergency_commands_.gear;  // tmp
431:   }
432: 
433:   // Check engage
434:   if (!is_engaged_) {
435:     filtered_commands.control.longitudinal = createLongitudinalStopControlCmd();
436:   }
437: 
438:   // Check pause. Place this check after all other checks as it needs the final output.
439:   adapi_pause_->update(filtered_commands.control);
440:   if (adapi_pause_->is_paused()) {
441:     if (is_engaged_) {
442:       filtered_commands.control.longitudinal = createLongitudinalStopControlCmd();
443:     } else {
444:       filtered_commands.control = createStopControlCmd();
445:     }
446:   }
447: 
448:   // Check if command filtering option is enable
449:   if (enable_cmd_limit_filter_) {
450:     // Apply limit filtering
451:     filtered_commands.control = filterControlCommand(filtered_commands.control);
452:   }
453:   // tmp: Publish vehicle emergency status
454:   VehicleEmergencyStamped vehicle_cmd_emergency;
455:   vehicle_cmd_emergency.emergency = (use_emergency_handling_ && is_system_emergency_);
456:   vehicle_cmd_emergency.stamp = filtered_commands.control.stamp;
457: 
458:   // Publish commands
459:   vehicle_cmd_emergency_pub_->publish(vehicle_cmd_emergency);
460:   control_cmd_pub_->publish(filtered_commands.control);
461:   published_time_publisher_->publish_if_subscribed(
462:     control_cmd_pub_, filtered_commands.control.stamp);
463:   adapi_pause_->publish();
464:   moderate_stop_interface_->publish();
465: 
466:   // Save ControlCmd to steering angle when disengaged
467:   prev_control_cmd_ = filtered_commands.control;
468: }

532: AckermannControlCommand VehicleCmdGate::filterControlCommand(const AckermannControlCommand & in)
533: {
534:   AckermannControlCommand out = in;
535:   const double dt = getDt();
536:   const auto mode = current_operation_mode_;
537:   const auto current_status_cmd = getActualStatusAsCommand();
538:   const auto ego_is_stopped = vehicle_stop_checker_->isVehicleStopped(stop_check_duration_);
539:   const auto input_cmd_is_stopping = in.longitudinal.acceleration < 0.0;
540: 
541:   filter_.setCurrentSpeed(current_kinematics_.twist.twist.linear.x);
542:   filter_on_transition_.setCurrentSpeed(current_kinematics_.twist.twist.linear.x);
543: 
544:   IsFilterActivated is_filter_activated;
545: 
546:   // Apply transition_filter when transiting from MANUAL to AUTO.
547:   if (mode.is_in_transition) {
548:     filter_on_transition_.filterAll(dt, current_steer_, out, is_filter_activated);
549:   } else {
550:     // When ego is stopped and the input command is not stopping,
551:     // use the higher of actual vehicle longitudinal state
552:     // and previous longitudinal command for the filtering
553:     // this is to prevent the jerk limits being applied and causing
554:     // a delay when restarting the vehicle.
555: 
556:     if (ego_is_stopped && !input_cmd_is_stopping) {
557:       auto prev_cmd = filter_.getPrevCmd();
558:       prev_cmd.longitudinal.acceleration =
559:         std::max(prev_cmd.longitudinal.acceleration, current_status_cmd.longitudinal.acceleration);
560:       // consider reverse driving
561:       prev_cmd.longitudinal.speed =
562:         std::fabs(prev_cmd.longitudinal.speed) > std::fabs(current_status_cmd.longitudinal.speed)
563:           ? prev_cmd.longitudinal.speed
564:           : current_status_cmd.longitudinal.speed;
565:       filter_.setPrevCmd(prev_cmd);
566:     }
567:     filter_.filterAll(dt, current_steer_, out, is_filter_activated);
568:   }
569: 
570:   // set prev value for both to keep consistency over switching:
571:   // Actual steer, vel, acc should be considered in manual mode to prevent sudden motion when
572:   // switching from manual to autonomous
573:   auto prev_values = mode.is_autoware_control_enabled ? out : current_status_cmd;
574: 
575:   if (ego_is_stopped) {
576:     prev_values.longitudinal = out.longitudinal;
577:   }
578: 
579:   // TODO(Horibe): To prevent sudden acceleration/deceleration when switching from manual to
580:   // autonomous, the filter should be applied for actual speed and acceleration during manual
581:   // driving. However, this means that the output command from Gate will always be close to the
582:   // driving state during manual driving. Here, let autoware publish the stop command when the ego
583:   // is stopped to intend the autoware is trying to keep stopping.
584: 
585:   filter_.setPrevCmd(prev_values);
586:   filter_on_transition_.setPrevCmd(prev_values);
587: 
588:   is_filter_activated.stamp = now();
589:   is_filter_activated_pub_->publish(is_filter_activated);
590:   publishMarkers(is_filter_activated);
591: 
592:   return out;
593: }

769: MarkerArray VehicleCmdGate::createMarkerArray(const IsFilterActivated & filter_activated)
770: {
771:   MarkerArray msg;
772: 
773:   if (!filter_activated.is_activated) {
774:     return msg;
775:   }
776: 
777:   /* add string marker */
778:   bool first_msg = true;
779:   std::string reason = "filter activated on";
780: 
781:   if (filter_activated.is_activated_on_acceleration) {
782:     reason += " lon_acc";
783:     first_msg = false;
784:   }
785:   if (filter_activated.is_activated_on_jerk) {
786:     reason += first_msg ? " jerk" : ", jerk";
787:     first_msg = false;
788:   }
789:   if (filter_activated.is_activated_on_speed) {
790:     reason += first_msg ? " speed" : ", speed";
791:     first_msg = false;
792:   }
793:   if (filter_activated.is_activated_on_steering) {
794:     reason += first_msg ? " steer" : ", steer";
795:     first_msg = false;
796:   }
797:   if (filter_activated.is_activated_on_steering_rate) {

334: class ControlCmdGenerator
335: {
336: public:
337:   CmdParams p_;  // used for sin wave command generation
338: 
339:   using Clock = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock;
340:   std::chrono::time_point<Clock> start_time_{Clock::now()};
341: 
342:   // generate ControlCommand with sin wave format.
343:   // TODO(Horibe): implement steering_rate and jerk command.
344:   AckermannControlCommand calcSinWaveCommand(bool reset_clock = false)
345:   {
346:     if (reset_clock) {
347:       start_time_ = Clock::now();
348:     }
349: 
350:     const auto dt_ns =
351:       std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(Clock::now() - start_time_);
352:     const auto dt_s = dt_ns.count() / 1e9;
353: 
354:     const auto sinWave = [&](auto amp, auto freq, auto bias) {
355:       return amp * std::sin(2.0 * M_PI * freq * dt_s + bias);
356:     };
357: 
358:     AckermannControlCommand cmd;
359:     cmd.lateral.steering_tire_angle = sinWave(p_.steering.max, p_.steering.freq, p_.steering.bias);
360:     cmd.longitudinal.speed =
361:       sinWave(p_.velocity.max, p_.velocity.freq, p_.velocity.bias) + p_.velocity.max;
362:     cmd.longitudinal.acceleration =
363:       sinWave(p_.acceleration.max, p_.acceleration.freq, p_.acceleration.bias);
364: 
365:     return cmd;
366:   }

We need to enable running the probabilistic occupancy grid map (OGM) with multiple LiDAR frames. Currently, the OGM pipeline supports only a single LiDAR frame. The goal is to add a synchronized fusion node that combines OGM outputs from multiple LiDAR sensors into a single fused map.

    The implementation should include:
    - A new launch file for the multi-LiDAR OGM method that creates individual OGM nodes for each LiDAR and a fusion node to combine their outputs.
    - A configuration file with parameters for each OGM creation and the fusion process (e.g., sensor topics, reliabilities, fusion method).
    - Updates to the existing pointcloud-based OGM node to allow `scan_origin_frame` to be empty, in which case it should use the input pointcloud's frame_id.
    - Updates to the fusion node to publish pipeline latency debug information.
    - Wiring the new method into the existing `probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map.launch.xml`.

    The new method should be selectable via the `occupancy_grid_map_method` launch argument with the value `multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map`.

## Environment Setup
Check the `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/CMakeLists.txt` to understand how this package is built and which dependencies are needed. For launcher-related changes, look at `launch/tier4_perception_launch/CMakeLists.txt`. The repository uses colcon for building; refer to the top-level `setup.cfg` for general project configuration. Test configurations may be found in `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/` (e.g., `test/` directory).

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create a new launch file** `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/launch/multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map.launch.py` that:
       - Loads a configuration file (YAML) containing shared parameters, per-LiDAR OGM creation parameters, and fusion parameters.
       - Validates that the lists of raw pointcloud topics, fusion input OGM topics, and reliabilities have the same length.
       - Instantiates a `pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map_node` per LiDAR, each subscribing to its corresponding raw pointcloud topic and publishing its own OGM.
       - Instantiates the `synchronized_grid_map_fusion_node` that subscribes to all per-LiDAR OGM topics and publishes the fused map.
       - Passes the appropriate parameters to each node (e.g., `map_frame`, `base_link_frame`, `gridmap_origin_frame`, map dimensions, etc.).
       - Supports `use_intra_process` and `use_multithread` launch arguments.

    2. **Create a sample configuration file** `perception/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map/config/multi_lidar_pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map.param.yaml` containing:
       - Shared parameters (map frame, base link frame, grid map origin frame, resolution, map dimensions).
       - OGM creation parameters (height filter, single-frame mode, grid map type).
       - Fusion parameters (raw pointcloud topics, fusion input OGM topics, reliabilities, fusion method).
       - Comments explaining each parameter group.

    3. **Update `pointcloud_based_occupancy_grid_map_node.cpp`** to make `scan_origin_frame` optional (default empty string). When empty, use the frame_id from the input raw pointcloud message before the TF lookup.

    4. **Update `synchronized_grid_map_fusion_node.cpp`** to compute and publish a `debug/pipeline_latency_ms` value similar to the existing `debug/cyclic_time_ms` and `debug/processing_time_ms` outputs. This should be based on the difference between the latest subscribed map's timestamp and the current node time.

    5. **Update `launch/tier4_perception_launch/launch/occupancy_grid_map/probabilistic_occupancy_grid_map.launch.xml`** to pass the `input/obstacle_pointcloud` argument to the new multi-LiDAR launch file.

327: OccupancyGridMapFixedBlindSpot GridMapFusionNode::SingleFrameOccupancyFusion(

329:   const builtin_interfaces::msg::Time latest_stamp, const std::vector<double> & weights)
330: {

346:   OccupancyGridMapFixedBlindSpot fused_map(
347:     occupancy_grid_maps[0].getSizeInCellsX(), occupancy_grid_maps[0].getSizeInCellsY(),
348:     occupancy_grid_maps[0].getResolution());
349:   fused_map.updateOrigin(
350:     gridmap_origin.position.x - fused_map.getSizeInMetersX() / 2,
351:     gridmap_origin.position.y - fused_map.getSizeInMetersY() / 2);
352: 
353:   // fix origin of each map
354:   for (auto & map : occupancy_grid_maps) {
355:     map.updateOrigin(fused_map.getOriginX(), fused_map.getOriginY());
356:   }

358:   // assume map is same size and resolutions
359:   for (unsigned int x = 0; x < fused_map.getSizeInCellsX(); x++) {
360:     for (unsigned int y = 0; y < fused_map.getSizeInCellsY(); y++) {
361:       // get cost of each map
362:       std::vector<unsigned char> costs;
363:       for (auto & map : occupancy_grid_maps) {

367:       // set fusion policy
368:       auto fused_cost = fusion_policy::singleFrameOccupancyFusion(costs, fusion_method_, weights);
369: 
370:       // set max cost to fused map
371:       fused_map.setCost(x, y, fused_cost);
372:     }
373:   }

`Centerpoint tiny` was trained in `Argoverse 2` (~110k lidar frames) [9] and TIER IV's internal database (~11k lidar frames) for 20 epochs.

### Training CenterPoint Model and Deploying to the Autoware

This section describes how to reproduce the process of training a CenterPoint model and converting it to the ONNX format used by this package.

Training is done with the forked mmdetection3d repository at <https://github.com/autowarefoundation/mmdetection3d> (not the original open-mmlab version). The fork adds several enhancements that are required for this workflow:

- Optional `PointPillar z` voxel feature
- PyTorch to ONNX converter
- `T4` format reader

#### Environment Setup

##### Install Miniconda

Install Miniconda by following the official instructions at <https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html>:

```bash
wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
```

##### Create a conda environment and install PyTorch

```bash
conda create -n open-mmlab python=3.8 -y
conda activate open-mmlab
```

Install PyTorch 1.13.1 with CUDA 11.6:

```bash
pip install torch==1.13.1+cu116 torchvision==0.14.1+cu116 --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu116
```

##### Install MMEngine, MMCV, and MMDetection via MIM

```bash
pip install openmim
mim install mmengine
mim install mmcv
mim install mmdet
```

Use the versions compatible with the forked mmdetection3d repository as described in its README.

##### Install the forked mmdetection3d repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/mmdetection3d.git
cd mmdetection3d
pip install -e .
```

#### (Optional) Docker Setup

As an alternative to the direct installation, you can build and run the Docker container provided by the forked mmdetection3d repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/mmdetection3d.git
cd mmdetection3d
docker build -t mmdetection3d .
docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace mmdetection3d
```

All of the instructions below can then be executed inside the container.

#### Dataset Preparation

##### nuScenes dataset

Download the `nuScenes` dataset from <https://www.nuscenes.org/nuscenes>. `nuScenes` full dataset includes `maps`, ` samples`, `sweeps`, and `v1.0-trainval` annotation files.

Extract the downloaded archives and create a symbolic link so that the dataset can be found by mmdetection3d:

```bash
mkdir -p data
ln -s /path/to/nuscenes data/nuscenes
```

Then run the data preparation script to create the required annotation files:

```bash
pip install nuscenes-devkit
python tools/create_data.py nuscenes --root-path ./data/nuscenes --out-dir ./data/nuscenes --extra-tag nuscenes
```

##### T4 format dataset

The fork also supports the `T4` format through its built-in `T4Dataset` reader. Prepare a `T4` dataset by running the data preparation script with the `annotation-hz` parameter to specify the annotation frequency:

```bash
python tools/create_data.py t4 --root-path ./data/t4 --out-dir ./data/t4 --extra-tag t4 --annotation-hz 2
```

#### Training

Train the CenterPoint model with the configuration used for this package:

```bash
python tools/train.py configs/centerpoint/centerpoint_pillar02_second_secfpn_head-circlenms_8xb4-cyclic-20e_nus-3d.py
```

The configuration is based on `PointPillars` with `SECOND` and `SECONDFPN` backbones and `CenterHead`. Adjust parameters such as `data_root`, `class_names`, `point_cloud_range`, and `evaluation` according to your dataset and requirements. The training checkpoints and logs are saved in `./work_dirs`.

#### Deployment

Since Autoware runs the model with TensorRT, the trained PyTorch model must first be converted to ONNX format. This step is critical.

Use the PyTorch to ONNX converter provided by the fork:

```bash
python tools/export.py configs/centerpoint/centerpoint_pillar02_second_secfpn_head-circlenms_8xb4-cyclic-20e_nus-3d.py ./work_dirs/<experiment>/latest.pth
```

The converter exports the network as ONNX files (a `VoxelFeatureEncoder` model and a `DetectionHead` model), corresponding to the `encoder_onnx_path` and `head_onnx_path` parameters of this package.

Verify the conversion by inspecting the exported ONNX files:

```bash
python -c "import onnx; onnx.checker.check_model(onnx.load('pts_voxel_encoder_centerpoint.onnx'))"
```

To deploy within Autoware, place the ONNX files on the path referenced by `encoder_onnx_path` and `head_onnx_path` in the launch configuration, and set `build_only:=true` to pre-build the TensorRT engine files from the ONNX files (see `The build_only option` section above).

### Changelog

+```

+##### Install MMEngine, MMCV, and MMDetection via MIM
+
+```bash
+pip install openmim
+mim install mmengine
+mim install mmcv
+mim install mmdet
+```
+
+Use the versions compatible with the forked mmdetection3d repository as described in its README.
+
+##### Install the forked mmdetection3d repository
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/mmdetection3d.git
+cd mmdetection3d
+pip install -e .
+```
+
+#### (Optional) Docker Setup
+
+As an alternative to the direct installation, you can build and run the Docker container provided by the forked mmdetection3d repository:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/mmdetection3d.git
+cd mmdetection3d
+docker build -t mmdetection3d .
+docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $(pwd):/workspace mmdetection3d
+```

+
+#### Dataset Preparation
+
+##### nuScenes dataset
+
+Download the `nuScenes` dataset from <https://www.nuscenes.org/nuscenes>. `nuScenes` full dataset includes `maps`, ` samples`, `sweeps`, and `v1.0-trainval` annotation files.

+Extract the downloaded archives and create a symbolic link so that the dataset can be found by mmdetection3d:
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p data
+ln -s /path/to/nuscenes data/nuscenes
+```
+
+Then run the data preparation script to create the required annotation files:
+
+```bash
+pip install nuscenes-devkit
+python tools/create_data.py nuscenes --root-path ./data/nuscenes --out-dir ./data/nuscenes --extra-tag nuscenes
+```
+
+##### T4 format dataset
+
+The fork also supports the `T4` format through its built-in `T4Dataset` reader. Prepare a `T4` dataset by running the data preparation script with the `annotation-hz` parameter to specify the annotation frequency:
+
+```bash

+```

+

+```

Adjust parameters such as `data_root`, `class_names`, `point_cloud_range`, and `evaluation` according to your dataset and requirements. The training checkpoints and logs are saved in `./work_dirs`.

+```

+The converter exports the network as ONNX files (a `VoxelFeatureEncoder` model and a `DetectionHead` model), corresponding to the `encoder_onnx_path` and `head_onnx_path` parameters of this package.

Implement a new ROS 2 node, `LidarMarkerLocalizer`, that estimates the vehicle's pose by detecting reflective markers (e.g., "reflector") in LiDAR pointcloud data and matching them against landmarks defined in a Lanelet2 map. The node should subscribe to the pointcloud, EKF pose, and map data, and publish the estimated pose with covariance. Also, integrate this node into the existing localization launch system so it can be selected as a pose source in `pose_twist_estimator.launch.xml` and `localization.launch.xml`.

    The goal is to provide an alternative pose estimation method based on fixed marker detection, useful in environments like tunnels where GNSS is unavailable.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repository files for build/install/test instructions:
    - `localization/autoware_landmark_based_localizer/autoware_lidar_marker_localizer/CMakeLists.txt` and `package.xml` for package configuration and dependencies
    - `launch/tier4_localization_launch/package.xml` for launch package dependencies
    - Root `setup.cfg` for general Python setup (if applicable)
    These files indicate the build system (ament_cmake) and required dependencies.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Create the package structure** under `localization/autoware_landmark_based_localizer/autoware_lidar_marker_localizer/`:
       - Create `CMakeLists.txt` to build a shared library and register a ROS 2 component node.
       - Create `package.xml` declaring dependencies (`rclcpp`, `pcl_ros`, `autoware_landmark_manager`, `localization_util`, etc.).
       - Create `src/lidar_marker_localizer.hpp` and `src/lidar_marker_localizer.cpp` for the `LidarMarkerLocalizer` class.
    2. **Implement the node logic**:
       - Subscribe to `~/input/pointcloud` (best-effort QoS), `~/input/ekf_pose`, and `~/input/lanelet2_map`.
       - Use `SmartPoseBuffer` to interpolate EKF pose with the pointcloud timestamp.
       - Load landmarks from the map using `autoware::landmark_manager::LandmarkManager`.
       - On each pointcloud:
         - Transform the pointcloud to the map frame using the interpolated pose.
         - Detect potential markers by analyzing high-intensity point patterns (using a pattern matching algorithm on a 2D grid, as described in the config `intensity_pattern`).
         - Validate detected markers against the nearest map landmark (distance check).
         - Compute the pose correction from the detected marker positions.
         - Publish the corrected pose on `~/output/pose_with_covariance` and debug topics (`~/debug/marker_detected`, `~/debug/marker_mapped`, `~/debug/marker_pointcloud`, `~/debug/pose_with_covariance`).
       - Implement a service `~/service/trigger_node_srv` (SetBool) to activate/deactivate the node.
       - Implement a diagnostics module for health reporting.
       - Add parameters for detection thresholds, marker dimensions, and logging (as seen in `config/lidar_marker_localizer.param.yaml`).
    3. **Add launch file** `launch/lidar_marker_localizer.launch.xml` within the new package to launch the node with configurable topic remapping.

187:       const Pose detected_marker_on_map =
188:         tier4_autoware_utils::transformPose(landmark.pose, self_pose);
189:       pose_array_msg.poses.push_back(detected_marker_on_map);
190:     }
191:     detected_tag_pose_pub_->publish(pose_array_msg);
192:   }
193: 
194:   // calc new_self_pose
195:   const Pose new_self_pose =
196:     landmark_manager_.calculate_new_self_pose(landmarks, self_pose, consider_orientation_);
197:   const Pose diff_pose = tier4_autoware_utils::inverseTransformPose(new_self_pose, self_pose);
198:   const double distance =
199:     std::hypot(diff_pose.position.x, diff_pose.position.y, diff_pose.position.z);
200: 
201:   // check distance
202:   if (distance > ekf_position_tolerance_) {
203:     RCLCPP_INFO_STREAM(this->get_logger(), "distance: " << distance);
204:     return;
205:   }
206:

208:   PoseWithCovarianceStamped pose_with_covariance_stamped;

211:   pose_with_covariance_stamped.pose.pose = new_self_pose;

215:   const double coeff = std::max(1.0, std::pow(distance / 5, 3));
216:   for (int i = 0; i < 36; i++) {
217:     pose_with_covariance_stamped.pose.covariance[i] = coeff * base_covariance_[i];
218:   }

228:     diag_status.level = diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::OK;
229:     diag_status.message = "AR tags detected. The number of tags: " + std::to_string(detected_tags);

241:   diag_status.values.push_back(key_value);

251: void ArTagBasedLocalizer::cam_info_callback(const CameraInfo::ConstSharedPtr & msg)
252: {
253:   if (cam_info_received_) {
254:     return;
255:   }
256: 
257:   // copy camera matrix
258:   cv::Mat camera_matrix(3, 4, CV_64FC1);
259:   std::copy(msg->p.begin(), msg->p.end(), camera_matrix.begin<double>());
260: 
261:   // all 0
262:   cv::Mat distortion_coeff(4, 1, CV_64FC1, 0.0);
263:

274:     ekf_pose_buffer_->push_back(msg);
275:   } else {
276:     RCLCPP_ERROR_STREAM_THROTTLE(
277:       get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000,
278:       "Received initial pose message with frame_id "
279:         << msg->header.frame_id << ", but expected map. "
280:         << "Please check the frame_id in the input topic and ensure it is correct.");
281:   }

284: std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark> ArTagBasedLocalizer::detect_landmarks(
285:   const Image::ConstSharedPtr & msg)
286: {
287:   const builtin_interfaces::msg::Time sensor_stamp = msg->header.stamp;
288: 
289:   // get image
290:   cv::Mat in_image;
291:   try {
292:     cv_bridge::CvImagePtr cv_ptr = cv_bridge::toCvCopy(*msg, sensor_msgs::image_encodings::RGB8);
293:     cv_ptr->image.copyTo(in_image);
294:   } catch (cv_bridge::Exception & e) {
295:     RCLCPP_ERROR(this->get_logger(), "cv_bridge exception: %s", e.what());
296:     return std::vector<Landmark>{};
297:   }
298: 
299:   // get transform from base_link to camera
300:   TransformStamped transform_sensor_to_base_link;
301:   try {
302:     transform_sensor_to_base_link =
303:       tf_buffer_->lookupTransform("base_link", msg->header.frame_id, sensor_stamp);
304:   } catch (tf2::TransformException & ex) {
305:     RCLCPP_INFO(this->get_logger(), "Could not transform base_link to camera: %s", ex.what());
306:     return std::vector<Landmark>{};
307:   }
308: 
309:   // detect
310:   std::vector<aruco::Marker> markers;
311:   detector_.detect(in_image, markers, cam_param_, marker_size_, false);
312: 
313:   // parse
314:   std::vector<Landmark> landmarks;
315: 
316:   for (aruco::Marker & marker : markers) {
317:     // convert marker pose to tf
318:     const cv::Quat<float> q = cv::Quat<float>::createFromRvec(marker.Rvec);
319:     Pose pose;
320:     pose.position.x = marker.Tvec.at<float>(0, 0);
321:     pose.position.y = marker.Tvec.at<float>(1, 0);
322:     pose.position.z = marker.Tvec.at<float>(2, 0);
323:     pose.orientation.x = q.x;
324:     pose.orientation.y = q.y;
325:     pose.orientation.z = q.z;
326:     pose.orientation.w = q.w;
327:     const double distance = std::hypot(pose.position.x, pose.position.y, pose.position.z);
328:     if (distance <= distance_threshold_) {
329:       tf2::doTransform(pose, pose, transform_sensor_to_base_link);
330:       landmarks.push_back(Landmark{std::to_string(marker.id), pose});
331:     }
332: 
333:     // for debug, drawing the detected markers
334:     marker.draw(in_image, cv::Scalar(0, 0, 255), 2);
335:     aruco::CvDrawingUtils::draw3dAxis(in_image, marker, cam_param_);
336:   }
337: 
338:   // for debug
339:   if (image_pub_->get_subscription_count() > 0) {
340:     cv_bridge::CvImage out_msg;
341:     out_msg.header.stamp = sensor_stamp;
342:     out_msg.encoding = sensor_msgs::image_encodings::RGB8;
343:     out_msg.image = in_image;
344:     image_pub_->publish(*out_msg.toImageMsg());
345:   }
346: 
347:   return landmarks;
348: }

211: void LidarMarkerLocalizer::main_process(const PointCloud2::ConstSharedPtr & points_msg_ptr)
212: {
213:   const builtin_interfaces::msg::Time sensor_ros_time = points_msg_ptr->header.stamp;
214: 
215:   // (0) Determine point cloud type
216:   const bool is_xyziradrt =
217:     autoware::pointcloud_preprocessor::utils::is_data_layout_compatible_with_point_xyziradrt(
218:       *points_msg_ptr);
219:   const bool is_xyzirc =
220:     autoware::pointcloud_preprocessor::utils::is_data_layout_compatible_with_point_xyzirc(
221:       *points_msg_ptr);
222: 
223:   if (!is_xyziradrt && !is_xyzirc) {
224:     RCLCPP_WARN_STREAM_THROTTLE(
225:       this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000,
226:       "Unknown point cloud type. Cannot process this point cloud.");
227:     return;
228:   }
229: 
230:   // (1) check if the map have be received
231:   const std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark> map_landmarks = landmark_manager_.get_landmarks();
232:   const bool is_received_map = !map_landmarks.empty();
233:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value("is_received_map", is_received_map);
234:   if (!is_received_map) {
235:     std::stringstream message;
236:     message << "Not receive the landmark information. Please check if the vector map is being "
237:             << "published and if the landmark information is correctly specified.";
238:     RCLCPP_INFO_STREAM_THROTTLE(this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, message.str());
239:     diagnostics_interface_->update_level_and_message(
240:       diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::WARN, message.str());
241:     return;
242:   }
243: 
244:   // (2) get Self Pose
245:   const std::optional<autoware::localization_util::SmartPoseBuffer::InterpolateResult>
246:     interpolate_result = ekf_pose_buffer_->interpolate(sensor_ros_time);
247: 
248:   const bool is_received_self_pose = interpolate_result != std::nullopt;
249:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value("is_received_self_pose", is_received_self_pose);
250:   if (!is_received_self_pose) {
251:     std::stringstream message;
252:     message << "Could not get self_pose. Please check if the self pose is being published and if "
253:             << "the timestamp of the self pose is correctly specified";
254:     RCLCPP_INFO_STREAM_THROTTLE(this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, message.str());
255:     diagnostics_interface_->update_level_and_message(
256:       diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::WARN, message.str());
257:     return;
258:   }
259: 
260:   ekf_pose_buffer_->pop_old(sensor_ros_time);
261:   const Pose self_pose = interpolate_result.value().interpolated_pose.pose.pose;
262: 
263:   // (3) detect marker
264:   std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark> detected_landmarks;
265:   if (is_xyziradrt) {
266:     detected_landmarks = detect_landmarks<autoware::point_types::PointXYZIRADRT>(points_msg_ptr);
267:   } else {
268:     detected_landmarks = detect_landmarks<autoware::point_types::PointXYZIRC>(points_msg_ptr);
269:   }
270: 
271:   const bool is_detected_marker = !detected_landmarks.empty();
272:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value("detect_marker_num", detected_landmarks.size());
273: 
274:   // (4) check distance to the nearest marker
275:   const landmark_manager::Landmark nearest_marker = get_nearest_landmark(self_pose, map_landmarks);
276:   const Pose nearest_marker_pose_on_base_link =
277:     autoware_utils::inverse_transform_pose(nearest_marker.pose, self_pose);
278: 
279:   const double distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker =
280:     std::abs(nearest_marker_pose_on_base_link.position.x);
281:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value(
282:     "distance_self_pose_to_nearest_marker", distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker);
283: 
284:   const double distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y =
285:     std::abs(nearest_marker_pose_on_base_link.position.y - param_.marker_to_vehicle_offset_y);
286:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value(
287:     "distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y", distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y);
288: 
289:   const bool is_exist_marker_within_self_pose =
290:     (distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker <
291:      param_.limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker) &&
292:     (distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y <
293:      param_.limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y);
294: 
295:   if (!is_detected_marker) {
296:     if (!is_exist_marker_within_self_pose) {
297:       std::stringstream message;
298:       message << "Could not detect marker, because the distance from self_pose to nearest_marker "
299:               << "is too far (" << distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker << " [m]).";
300:       diagnostics_interface_->update_level_and_message(
301:         diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::OK, message.str());
302:     } else {
303:       std::stringstream message;
304:       message << "Could not detect marker, although the distance from self_pose to nearest_marker "
305:               << "is near (" << distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker << " [m]).";
306:       RCLCPP_INFO_STREAM_THROTTLE(this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, message.str());
307:       diagnostics_interface_->update_level_and_message(
308:         diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::WARN, message.str());
309:     }
310:     return;
311:   }
312: 
313:   // for debug
314:   if (pub_marker_detected_->get_subscription_count() > 0) {
315:     PoseArray pose_array_msg;
316:     pose_array_msg.header.stamp = sensor_ros_time;
317:     pose_array_msg.header.frame_id = "map";
318:     for (const landmark_manager::Landmark & landmark : detected_landmarks) {
319:       const Pose detected_marker_on_map = autoware_utils::transform_pose(landmark.pose, self_pose);
320:       pose_array_msg.poses.push_back(detected_marker_on_map);
321:     }
322:     pub_marker_detected_->publish(pose_array_msg);
323:   }
324: 
325:   // (4) calculate diff pose
326:   const Pose new_self_pose =
327:     landmark_manager_.calculate_new_self_pose(detected_landmarks, self_pose, false);
328: 
329:   const double diff_x = new_self_pose.position.x - self_pose.position.x;
330:   const double diff_y = new_self_pose.position.y - self_pose.position.y;
331: 
332:   const double diff_norm = std::hypot(diff_x, diff_y);
333:   const bool is_exist_marker_within_lanelet2_map =
334:     diff_norm < param_.limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_marker;
335: 
336:   diagnostics_interface_->add_key_value("distance_lanelet2_marker_to_detected_marker", diff_norm);
337:   if (!is_exist_marker_within_lanelet2_map) {
338:     std::stringstream message;
339:     message << "The distance from lanelet2 to the detect marker is too far(" << diff_norm
340:             << " [m]). The limit is " << param_.limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_marker << ".";
341:     RCLCPP_INFO_STREAM_THROTTLE(this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, message.str());
342:     diagnostics_interface_->update_level_and_message(
343:       diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticStatus::WARN, message.str());
344:     return;
345:   }
346: 
347:   const landmark_manager::Landmark nearest_detected_landmark =
348:     get_nearest_landmark(self_pose, detected_landmarks);
349: 
350:   if (is_xyziradrt) {
351:     save_intensity<autoware::point_types::PointXYZIRADRT>(
352:       points_msg_ptr, nearest_detected_landmark.pose);
353:   } else {
354:     save_intensity<autoware::point_types::PointXYZIRC>(
355:       points_msg_ptr, nearest_detected_landmark.pose);
356:   }
357: 
358:   // (5) Apply diff pose to self pose
359:   // only x and y is changed
360:   PoseWithCovarianceStamped result;
361:   result.header.stamp = sensor_ros_time;
362:   result.header.frame_id = "map";
363:   result.pose.pose.position.x = new_self_pose.position.x;
364:   result.pose.pose.position.y = new_self_pose.position.y;
365:   result.pose.pose.position.z = new_self_pose.position.z;
366:   result.pose.pose.orientation = self_pose.orientation;
367: 
368:   // set covariance
369:   const Eigen::Quaterniond map_to_base_link_quat = Eigen::Quaterniond(
370:     result.pose.pose.orientation.w, result.pose.pose.orientation.x, result.pose.pose.orientation.y,
371:     result.pose.pose.orientation.z);
372:   const Eigen::Matrix3d map_to_base_link_rotation =
373:     map_to_base_link_quat.normalized().toRotationMatrix();
374:   result.pose.covariance = rotate_covariance(param_.base_covariance, map_to_base_link_rotation);
375: 
376:   pub_base_link_pose_with_covariance_on_map_->publish(result);
377:   pub_debug_pose_with_covariance_->publish(result);
378: 
379:   // for debug
380:   const auto marker_pointcloud_msg_ptr =
381:     extract_marker_pointcloud(points_msg_ptr, nearest_detected_landmark.pose);
382:   pub_marker_pointcloud_->publish(*marker_pointcloud_msg_ptr);
383: 
384:   // save log
385:   if (param_.enable_save_log) {
386:     save_detected_marker_log(marker_pointcloud_msg_ptr);
387:   }
388: }

414: template <typename PointT>
415: std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark> LidarMarkerLocalizer::detect_landmarks(
416:   const PointCloud2::ConstSharedPtr & points_msg_ptr)
417: {
418:   // TODO(YamatoAndo)
419:   // Transform sensor_frame to base_link
420:   typename pcl::PointCloud<PointT>::Ptr points_ptr(new pcl::PointCloud<PointT>);
421:   pcl::fromROSMsg(*points_msg_ptr, *points_ptr);
422: 
423:   if (points_ptr->empty()) {
424:     RCLCPP_WARN_STREAM_THROTTLE(this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, "No points!");
425:     return std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark>{};
426:   }
427: 
428:   // Use parameters for initial lower/upper ring id
429:   uint16_t lower_ring_id = static_cast<uint16_t>(param_.lower_ring_id_init);
430:   uint16_t upper_ring_id = static_cast<uint16_t>(param_.upper_ring_id_init);
431:   for (const auto & point : points_ptr->points) {
432:     lower_ring_id = std::min(get_ring_id(point), lower_ring_id);
433:     upper_ring_id = std::max(get_ring_id(point), upper_ring_id);
434:   }
435:   uint16_t ring_num = upper_ring_id - lower_ring_id + 1;
436: 
437:   std::vector<pcl::PointCloud<PointT>> ring_points(ring_num);
438: 
439:   float min_x = std::numeric_limits<float>::max();
440:   float max_x = std::numeric_limits<float>::lowest();
441:   for (const auto & point : points_ptr->points) {
442:     ring_points[get_ring_id(point) - lower_ring_id].push_back(point);
443:     min_x = std::min(min_x, point.x);
444:     max_x = std::max(max_x, point.x);
445:   }
446: 
447:   // Check that the leaf size is not too small, given the size of the data
448:   const int bin_num = static_cast<int>((max_x - min_x) / param_.resolution + 1);
449: 
450:   if (bin_num < static_cast<int>(param_.intensity_pattern.size())) {
451:     RCLCPP_WARN_STREAM_THROTTLE(
452:       this->get_logger(), *this->get_clock(), 1000, "bin_num is too small!");
453:     return std::vector<landmark_manager::Landmark>{};
454:   }
455: 
456:   // initialize variables
457:   constexpr int max_vote_percentage = 100;  // Maximum vote percentage for visualization
458:   std::vector<int> vote(bin_num, 0);
459:   std::vector<float> reference_ring_y(bin_num, std::numeric_limits<float>::max());
460: 
461:   nav_msgs::msg::OccupancyGrid center_intensity_grid_msg;
462:   center_intensity_grid_msg.header = points_msg_ptr->header;
463:   center_intensity_grid_msg.header.frame_id = "base_link";

57: 
58: ```plantuml
59: @startuml
60: 
61: group main process
62:   start
63:   if (Receive a map?) then (yes)
64:   else (no)
65:     stop
66:   endif

82:       stop

84:     else (no)

arguments.content:
# LiDAR Marker Localizer

**LidarMarkerLocalizer** is a detect-reflector-based localization node.

The node estimates the vehicle's pose by detecting reflective markers (e.g., `reflector`) in LiDAR
pointcloud data and matching them against landmarks defined in a Lanelet2 map. It is intended as an
alternative pose estimation method for environments where GNSS is unavailable, such as tunnels.

## Inputs / Outputs

### `lidar_marker_localizer` node

#### Input

| Name                   | Type                                            | Description                  |
| :--------------------- | :---------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| `~/input/lanelet2_map` | `autoware_auto_mapping_msgs::msg::HADMapBin`    | Data of lanelet2             |
| `~/input/pointcloud`   | `sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2`                 | PointType: `PointXYZIRADRT`  |
| `~/input/ekf_pose`     | `geometry_msgs::msg::PoseWithCovarianceStamped` | EKF Pose                     |

#### Output

| Name                            | Type                                            | Description         |
| :------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------- | :------------------ |
| `~/output/pose_with_covariance` | `geometry_msgs::msg::PoseWithCovarianceStamped` | Estimated pose      |
| `/diagnostics`                  | `diagnostic_msgs::msg::DiagnosticArray`         | Diagnostics outputs |

##### For debug

| Name                            | Type                                            | Description                                          |
| :------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------- |
| `~/debug/pose_with_covariance`  | `geometry_msgs::msg::PoseWithCovarianceStamped` | Estimated pose                                       |
| `~/debug/marker_detected`       | `geometry_msgs::msg::PoseArray`                 | Detected marker poses                                |
| `~/debug/marker_mapped`         | `visualization_msgs::msg::MarkerArray`          | Loaded landmarks to visualize in Rviz as thin boards |
| `~/debug/marker_pointcloud`     | `sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2`                 | PointCloud of the detected marker                    |

#### Service

| Name                      | Type                  | Description                                    |
| :------------------------ | :-------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- |
| `~/service/trigger_node_srv` | `std_srvs::srv::SetBool` | Activate/deactivate the node. When activated, the buffered EKF poses are cleared. |


## Parameters

| Name                                            | Type   | Default                                                | Description                                                                 |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :----- | :----------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `marker_name`                                   | string | `reflector`                                            | The name of the markers listed in the HD map                                |
| `resolution`                                    | double | `0.05`                                                 | Grid size for marker detection algorithm [m]                                |
| `intensity_pattern`                             | array  | `[-1, -1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1]`               | A sequence of high/low intensity to perform pattern matching                |
| `match_intensity_difference_threshold`          | int    | `20`                                                   | Threshold for determining high/low intensity                                |
| `positive_match_num_threshold`                  | int    | `3`                                                    | Threshold for the number of required positive matches                       |
| `negative_match_num_threshold`                  | int    | `3`                                                    | Threshold for the number of required negative matches                       |
| `vote_threshold_for_detect_marker`              | int    | `20`                                                   | Threshold for the number of rings matching the pattern needed to detect a marker |
| `marker_to_vehicle_offset_y`                    | double | `0.0`                                                  | Y-axis offset from the center of the marker to vehicle [m]                  |
| `marker_height_from_ground`                     | double | `1.075`                                                | Height from the ground to the center of the marker [m]                      |
| `lower_ring_id_init`                            | int    | `128`                                                  | Initial value when searching for the lowest ring ID within the point cloud  |
| `upper_ring_id_init`                            | int    | `0`                                                    | Initial value when searching for the highest ring ID within the point cloud |
| `reference_ring_number`                         | int    | `255`                                                  | Reference ring number when detecting the marker. Set `255` to disable ring filtering |
| `self_pose_timeout_sec`                         | double | `1.0`                                                  | Timeout for self pose [sec]                                                 |
| `self_pose_distance_tolerance_m`                | double | `1.0`                                                  | Tolerance for the distance between two points when performing linear interpolation [m] |
| `limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker` | double | `2.0`  | Distance limit for determining whether the node should detect a marker [m]  |
| `limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_nearest_marker_y` | double | `1.0` | Y-axis distance limit for determining whether the node should detect a marker [m] |
| `limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_marker`       | double | `2.0`                                                  | Distance limit for avoiding miss detection [m]                              |
| `base_covariance`                               | array  | see below                                              | Output covariance in the base_link coordinate                               |
| `marker_width`                                  | double | `0.8`                                                  | Width of a marker. Used for visualizing the detected marker pointcloud [m]  |
| `enable_save_log`                               | bool   | `false`                                                | Whether to save the pointcloud of the detected marker as a CSV log          |
| `save_file_directory_path`                      | string | `detected_reflector_intensity`                         | Directory path to save the detected marker logs                             |
| `save_file_name`                                | string | `detected_reflector_intensity`                         | Base file name of the detected marker logs                                  |
| `save_frame_id`                                 | string | `velodyne_top`                                         | Frame in which the detected marker logs are saved                           |
| `radius_for_extracting_marker_pointcloud`       | double | `0.4`                                                  | Radius for extracting the marker pointcloud [m]                             |
| `queue_size_for_output_pose`                    | int    | `10`                                                   | Queue size for output/pose_with_covariance publisher                        |
| `queue_size_for_debug_pub_msg`                  | int    | `10`                                                   | Queue size for debug publishers                                             |

## How to launch

When launching Autoware, set `lidar-marker` for `pose_source`.

```bash
ros2 launch autoware_launch ... \
    pose_source:=lidar-marker \
    ...
```

## Design

### Flowchart

```plantuml
@startuml

group main process
  start
  if (Receive a map?) then (yes)
  else (no)
    stop
  endif

  if (Receive a self pose?) then (yes)
  else (no)
    stop
  endif

  :Interpolate based on the received ego-vehicle's positions to align with sensor time;

  :Detect markers (see "Detection Algorithm");

  if (Find markers?) then (yes)
  else (no)
    if (the distance from the ego-vehicle's position to the nearest marker's position on the lanelet2 map is nearby?) then (yes)
      stop
      note : Error. It should have been able to detect marker
    else (no)
      stop
      note : Not Error. There are no markers around the ego-vehicle
    endif
  endif

  :Calculate the correction amount from the ego-vehicle's position;

  if (Is the found marker's position close to the one on the lanelet2 map?) then (yes)
  else (no)
    stop
    note : Detected something that isn't a marker
  endif

  :Publish result;

  stop
end group

@enduml

```

## Detection Algorithm

1. Split the LiDAR point cloud into rings along the x-axis of the base_link coordinate system at
   intervals of the `resolution` size.
2. Find the portion of intensity that matches the `intensity_pattern`.
3. Perform steps 1 and 2 for each ring, accumulate the matching indices, and detect portions where
   the count exceeds the `vote_threshold_for_detect_marker` as markers.
4. Match the detected markers against the landmarks on the lanelet2 map, validate the corrected pose
   using `limit_distance_from_self_pose_to_marker`, and publish the pose.
